#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

#include "nvs_flash.h"

#include "esp_mac.h"
#include "rom/ets_sys.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_wifi.h"
#include "esp_netif.h"
#include "esp_now.h"
#include "esp_csi_gain_ctrl.h"

#define CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL   11
#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61 || (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 && ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(5, 4, 0))
#define CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE               WIFI_BAND_MODE_2G_ONLY
#define CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS           WIFI_BW_HT40
#define CONFIG_WIFI_5G_BANDWIDTHS           WIFI_BW_HT40
#define CONFIG_WIFI_2G_PROTOCOL             WIFI_PROTOCOL_11N
#define CONFIG_WIFI_5G_PROTOCOL             WIFI_PROTOCOL_11N
#else
#define CONFIG_WIFI_BANDWIDTH           WIFI_BW_HT40
#endif

#define CONFIG_ESP_NOW_PHYMODE           WIFI_PHY_MODE_HT40
#define CONFIG_ESP_NOW_RATE             WIFI_PHY_RATE_MCS0_LGI
#define CONFIG_FORCE_GAIN                   0

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
#define CSI_FORCE_LLTF                      0
#endif

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32S3 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C3 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
#define CONFIG_GAIN_CONTROL                 1
#endif

#if ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(6, 0, 0)
#define ESP_IF_WIFI_STA ESP_MAC_WIFI_STA
#endif

static const uint8_t CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC[] = {0x1a, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00};
static const char *TAG = "csi_recv";

static void wifi_init()
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_event_loop_create_default());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_netif_init());
    wifi_init_config_t cfg = WIFI_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_init(&cfg));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_STA));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_storage(WIFI_STORAGE_RAM));

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());
    esp_wifi_set_band_mode(CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE);
    wifi_protocols_t protocols = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_PROTOCOL,
        .ghz_5g = CONFIG_WIFI_5G_PROTOCOL
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_protocols(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &protocols));
    wifi_bandwidths_t bandwidth = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS,
        .ghz_5g = CONFIG_WIFI_5G_BANDWIDTHS
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_bandwidths(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &bandwidth));
#elif (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 && ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(5, 4, 0)) || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());
    esp_wifi_set_band_mode(CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE);
    wifi_protocols_t protocols = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_PROTOCOL,
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_protocols(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &protocols));
    wifi_bandwidths_t bandwidth = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS,
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_bandwidths(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &bandwidth));
#else
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_bandwidth(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, CONFIG_WIFI_BANDWIDTH));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());
#endif

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_NONE));
#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5
    if ((CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE == WIFI_BAND_MODE_2G_ONLY && CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS == WIFI_BW_HT20)
            || (CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE == WIFI_BAND_MODE_5G_ONLY && CONFIG_WIFI_5G_BANDWIDTHS == WIFI_BW_HT20)) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE));
    } else {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_BELOW));
    }
#elif (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 && ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(5, 4, 0)) || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    if (CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE == WIFI_BAND_MODE_2G_ONLY && CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS == WIFI_BW_HT20) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE));
    } else {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_BELOW));
    }
#else
    if (CONFIG_WIFI_BANDWIDTH == WIFI_BW_HT20) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE));
    } else {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_BELOW));
    }
#endif

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_mac(WIFI_IF_STA, CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC));
}

static void wifi_esp_now_init(esp_now_peer_info_t peer)
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_init());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_set_pmk((uint8_t *)"pmk1234567890123"));
    esp_now_rate_config_t rate_config = {
        .phymode = CONFIG_ESP_NOW_PHYMODE,
        .rate = CONFIG_ESP_NOW_RATE,//  WIFI_PHY_RATE_MCS0_LGI,
        .ersu = false,
        .dcm = false
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_add_peer(&peer));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_set_peer_rate_config(peer.peer_addr, &rate_config));

}

static void wifi_csi_rx_cb(void *ctx, wifi_csi_info_t *info)
{
    if (!info || !info->buf) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "<%s> wifi_csi_cb", esp_err_to_name(ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG));
        return;
    }

    if (memcmp(info->mac, CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC, 6)) {
        return;
    }

    const wifi_pkt_rx_ctrl_t *rx_ctrl = &info->rx_ctrl;
    static int s_count = 0;
    float compensate_gain = 1.0f;
    static uint8_t agc_gain = 0;
    static int8_t fft_gain = 0;
#if CONFIG_GAIN_CONTROL
    static uint8_t agc_gain_baseline = 0;
    static int8_t fft_gain_baseline = 0;
    esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_rx_gain(rx_ctrl, &agc_gain, &fft_gain);
    if (s_count < 100) {
        esp_csi_gain_ctrl_record_rx_gain(agc_gain, fft_gain);
    } else if (s_count == 100) {
        esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_rx_gain_baseline(&agc_gain_baseline, &fft_gain_baseline);
#if CONFIG_FORCE_GAIN
        esp_csi_gain_ctrl_set_rx_force_gain(agc_gain_baseline, fft_gain_baseline);
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "fft_force %d, agc_force %d", fft_gain_baseline, agc_gain_baseline);
#endif
    }
    esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_gain_compensation(&compensate_gain, agc_gain, fft_gain);
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "compensate_gain %f, agc_gain %d, fft_gain %d", compensate_gain, agc_gain, fft_gain);
#endif

    uint32_t rx_id = *(uint32_t *)(info->payload + 15);
#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    if (!s_count) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "================ CSI RECV ================");
        ets_printf("type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_format,len,first_word,data\n");
    }

    ets_printf("CSI_DATA,%d," MACSTR ",%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d",
               rx_id, MAC2STR(info->mac), rx_ctrl->rssi, rx_ctrl->rate,
               rx_ctrl->noise_floor, fft_gain, agc_gain,  rx_ctrl->channel,
               rx_ctrl->timestamp, rx_ctrl->sig_len, rx_ctrl->cur_bb_format);
#else
    if (!s_count) {
        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "================ CSI RECV ================");
        ets_printf("type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_format,len,first_word,data\n");
    }

    ets_printf("CSI_DATA,%d," MACSTR ",%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d",
               rx_id, MAC2STR(info->mac), rx_ctrl->rssi, rx_ctrl->rate, rx_ctrl->sig_mode,
               rx_ctrl->mcs, rx_ctrl->cwb, rx_ctrl->smoothing, rx_ctrl->not_sounding,
               rx_ctrl->aggregation, rx_ctrl->stbc, rx_ctrl->fec_coding, rx_ctrl->sgi,
               rx_ctrl->noise_floor, rx_ctrl->ampdu_cnt, rx_ctrl->channel, rx_ctrl->secondary_channel,
               rx_ctrl->timestamp, rx_ctrl->ant, rx_ctrl->sig_len, rx_ctrl->sig_mode);

#endif
#if (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61) && CSI_FORCE_LLTF
    int16_t csi = ((int16_t)(((((uint16_t)info->buf[1]) << 8) | info->buf[0]) << 4) >> 4);
    ets_printf(",%d,%d,\"[%d", (info->len - 2) / 2, info->first_word_invalid, (int16_t)(compensate_gain * csi));
    for (int i = 2; i < (info->len - 2); i += 2) {
        csi = ((int16_t)(((((uint16_t)info->buf[i + 1]) << 8) | info->buf[i]) << 4) >> 4);
        ets_printf(",%d", (int16_t)(compensate_gain * csi));
    }
#else
    ets_printf(",%d,%d,\"[%d", info->len, info->first_word_invalid, (int16_t)(compensate_gain * info->buf[0]));
    for (int i = 1; i < info->len; i++) {
        ets_printf(",%d", (int16_t)(compensate_gain * info->buf[i]));
    }
#endif
    ets_printf("]\"\n");
    s_count++;
}

static void wifi_csi_init()
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_promiscuous(true));

    /**< default config */
#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    wifi_csi_config_t csi_config = {
        .enable                   = true,
        .acquire_csi_legacy       = false,
        .acquire_csi_force_lltf   = CSI_FORCE_LLTF,
        .acquire_csi_ht20         = true,
        .acquire_csi_ht40         = true,
        .acquire_csi_vht          = false,
        .acquire_csi_su           = false,
        .acquire_csi_mu           = false,
        .acquire_csi_dcm          = false,
        .acquire_csi_beamformed   = false,
        .acquire_csi_he_stbc_mode = 2,
        .val_scale_cfg            = 0,
        .dump_ack_en              = false,
        .reserved                 = false
    };
#elif CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6
    wifi_csi_config_t csi_config = {
        .enable                 = true,
        .acquire_csi_legacy     = false,
        .acquire_csi_ht20       = true,
        .acquire_csi_ht40       = true,
        .acquire_csi_su         = true,
        .acquire_csi_mu         = true,
        .acquire_csi_dcm        = true,
        .acquire_csi_beamformed = true,
        .acquire_csi_he_stbc    = 2,
        .val_scale_cfg          = false,
        .dump_ack_en            = false,
        .reserved               = false
    };
#else
    wifi_csi_config_t csi_config = {
        .lltf_en           = true,
        .htltf_en          = true,
        .stbc_htltf2_en    = true,
        .ltf_merge_en      = true,
        .channel_filter_en = true,
        .manu_scale        = false,
        .shift             = false,
    };
#endif
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_csi_config(&csi_config));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb(wifi_csi_rx_cb, NULL));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_csi(true));
}

void app_main()
{
    /**
     * @brief Initialize NVS
     */
    esp_err_t ret = nvs_flash_init();
    if (ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES || ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(nvs_flash_erase());
        ret = nvs_flash_init();
    }
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(ret);

    /**
     * @brief Initialize Wi-Fi
     */
    wifi_init();

    /**
     * @brief Initialize ESP-NOW
     *        ESP-NOW protocol see: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/api-reference/network/esp_now.html
     */

    esp_now_peer_info_t peer = {
        .channel   = CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL,
        .ifidx     = WIFI_IF_STA,
        .encrypt   = false,
        .peer_addr = {0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff},
    };

    wifi_esp_now_init(peer);

    wifi_csi_init();
}

I notice the rx_id is pulled from a fixed offset in the ESP-NOW payload, and the receive example has a couple of quirks: it mislabels sig_mode as rx_format, and logs every packet when gain control is enabled, which could be costly. I should check the remaining config files for more context.

I should avoid heavy printf calls inside the callback since that's expensive, like the official implementation does. Instead, I'll have the callback just tally counts and queue data, while a separate task handles periodic stats logging and printing.

For planning, I'll organize the work into roughly four features matching the milestones: firmware + backend parsing/CLI (M1), signal processing and dashboard (M2), calibration/recording/replay (M3), and fall detection with alerts/simulation/export (M4+M5), noting the gain-control component needs network access only at install time via the component manager.

I'm sketching the repo layout as top-level `backend/`, `dashboard/`, and `simulation/` Python packages with tests under `tests/`, a single CLI entrypoint, and Makefile targets for setup/test/dashboard/monitor, plus a `CSIPacket` dataclass and a `parse_line` function that returns a packet or raises a counted parse error.

For amplitude extraction, I'm reasoning through how ESP32 CSI data is structured as imaginary/real pairs per subcarrier, and deciding to consistently use the first 64 subcarriers (LLTF) across packet lengths so feature extraction stays uniform regardless of HT20/HT40 variations.

For serial communication, the receiver needs 921600 baud matching the ESP console config, and I need to account for XIAO ESP32-S3 using USB-Serial-JTAG instead of a traditional UART bridge.

Since not all S3 boards use native USB, I should offer an optional usb_jtag sdkconfig defaults file users can layer in with the multi-file SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS flag, and document the exact idf.py invocation. I also want to verify that esp_rom_printf gets properly routed through USB-Serial-JTAG when that's the selected console, since early boot messages depend on this being wired correctly.

I'm also running the numbers on throughput: at 100 Hz with 384 values and roughly 4 characters each, that's about 150 KB/s of data, which already exceeds what a 921600 baud UART (~92 KB/s) can sustain for HT40 mode. That seems concerning since official examples claim 100Hz works, so I'm double-checking the actual packet size including headers.

Given this bottleneck, I'm considering whether the receiver should default to a lower rate like 50 Hz, or add a Kconfig option to output only the LLTF portion to cut the data size while keeping the official packet format intact, since minimizing changes to the established format is preferable.

For the callback itself, it copies the control info, MAC address, length, and buffer bytes into a FreeRTOS queue using a non-blocking send so processing stays decoupled from the ISR context.

For stats output, I'll have the device print a line prefixed with "EG_STATS," containing uptime, total received frames, queue drops, and sequence gaps, so the Python parser can distinguish it from CSI data lines. The transmitter similarly prints "EG_TX_STATS," with sent/fail counts once per second, and I'm noting that the sequence ID is extracted from a fixed offset within the payload data.

I'm keeping the gain-control component for CSI compensation even though it requires network access during build, but stripping out the per-packet logging to reduce noise -- only C5/C6 variants will output fft_gain/agc_gain fields. The gain control include stays unconditional since the component should still build fine for classic ESP32 targets even without CONFIG_GAIN_CONTROL defined.

Since there's no ESP-IDF toolchain available here, I can't actually compile the firmware to verify it. Installing ESP-IDF would mean a ~1-2GB download into the home directory, which feels too invasive given the orchestrator's guidance to document install steps rather than assume the environment exists -- so I'll leave the firmware as unverified-compile and flag that as a known limitation rather than installing the full toolchain myself.

I'm also thinking through device detection tooling -- a script to list serial ports with VID/PID info to distinguish Espressif boards from CP210x, CH34x, or FTDI adapters, plus instructions for using esptool's chip_id command as a read-only check, noting that it still resets the board so users should be careful about which boards stay connected during testing.

For flashing, I'm planning simple commands like `idf.py flash monitor` tied to explicit port arguments, possibly wrapped in a script that requires confirmation and prints the chip ID before proceeding. Then for the packet processing pipeline, I'm working out how to extract amplitudes per subcarrier while masking out DC and guard band indices specific to the LLTF 64-subcarrier layout.

I'm mapping the ESP32's subcarrier index ordering to actual 802.11 frequency positions, figuring out which indices correspond to valid data subcarriers versus DC/null/guard subcarriers, and accounting for the first-word-invalid flag that can mark the first couple of subcarriers as unreliable. After building that fixed mask, I'm thinking through denoising options -- applying a Hampel or median filter per subcarrier followed by smoothing via EMA or a low-pass filter over a sliding window.

Now I'm designing the motion detection pipeline: normalizing amplitude per packet to counter AGC gain variance, then computing a motion score from a blend of per-subcarrier variance over a sliding window, deviation from a calibrated baseline profile (z-scored), and first-difference energy, all scaled so empty-room readings sit near a score of 1. I'm also defining data quality checks like minimum packet rate, sequence gap rate, RSSI range, and window fill, and sketching out the classification states -- unknown, empty/low, movement, rapid movement, and potential fall tied into a separate fall detector.

Now I'm working through the fall-detection heuristic itself: a state machine that flags a spike when the motion score crosses a rapid-movement threshold, then checks whether the score drops below a low threshold and stays there for several seconds afterward to confirm a potential fall. I'm deciding to keep configuration as plain dataclasses serialized to JSON rather than pulling in pydantic, and working out how calibration data should be persisted per sensor using a key derived from transmitter MAC, channel, bandwidth, and receiver identifiers.

For recordings, I'm designing a session folder structure with metadata plus per-label CSV files that store the raw line alongside parsed fields so replay can run through the same parser, and planning a ReplaySource that reads these files back and emits lines with original timing adjusted by a speed factor.

All three sources—serial, replay, and simulation—should emit lines in the same official CSI_DATA text format so they share one parsing pipeline, with simulated packets clearly flagged synthetic via a distinct MAC and "SIMULATED" source label.

For the dashboard, I'm thinking Streamlit needs a background acquisition thread held in a cached singleton Engine (source → parser → buffer → processor → detector), with the UI polling engine state via a periodically-refreshing fragment rather than blocking the main script.

I'm pinning dependency versions (numpy, scipy, pandas, pyserial, streamlit, plotly, pytest) for Python 3.11/3.12 compatibility, and planning a CLI with `ports`, `monitor`, `record`, and `fixture` replay commands that print live packet stats and amplitude bars. For testing I want fixture files with official-format sample lines that are clearly marked as non-real data.

For version control, since the workspace isn't a git repo yet, I'll run `git init` without making any commits, so the semantic reviewer can inspect files directly via `git status` rather than requiring a `git diff` against a committed baseline.

For the .gitignore, I need to exclude the .venv, firmware build directories, the generated sdkconfig, managed_components, and any recordings data, while keeping a .gitkeep placeholder. Now I'm finalizing the plan with four features and setting up the task context directory path.
I don't think I need to dig into the README details on C5/C6 or rx_state, so I'll move on to writing the files.

<user_instruction>
# Build EchoGuard — Wi-Fi CSI Fall Detection Prototype

You are my senior embedded systems, RF sensing, Python, and machine learning engineer.

Build a functional, hackathon-ready prototype called **EchoGuard**, a privacy-preserving, camera-free fall detection system that uses Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) to detect human movement.

**Priority: Get a working, real-hardware sensing prototype as quickly as possible. Do not spend time polishing features before the sensing pipeline works.**

## 1. Available Hardware

- Two ESP32 development boards, at least one potentially being a Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3.
- A third ESP32 is available but has existing firmware that must NOT be erased or modified.
- MacBook running macOS with Python available.
- Raspberry Pi available as an optional processing device.
- USB cables for programming and collecting data.

First, inspect the local environment, available tools, ESP-IDF installation, and connected serial devices. Identify the exact ESP32 chips before choosing firmware targets.

Do not automatically flash any device. Show me the detected devices and provide explicit commands for flashing the two selected boards.

**Design for two ESP32s by default. Never require a third board or external router.**

## 2. System Architecture

The system should operate completely offline after installation.

- ESP32 #1: Wi-Fi transmitter
- ESP32 #2: CSI receiver
- MacBook: CSI processing, recording, detection, visualization, and alerts
- Raspberry Pi: Optional alternative host, not required

Use the ESP32 transmitter to send Wi-Fi packets to the receiver at a consistent rate. Extract actual CSI measurements from the receiving ESP32 and stream them over USB serial to the MacBook.

Prefer the official Espressif repository:

https://github.com/espressif/esp-csi

Use its `csi_send` and `csi_recv` examples as the starting point.

Do not invent unsupported firmware APIs or implement an unnecessary Wi-Fi mesh network.

## 3. Firmware

Set up separate transmitter and receiver firmware projects.

The transmitter should:
- Send packets frequently enough to capture human motion.
- Operate without internet connectivity.
- Use an appropriate fixed Wi-Fi channel.
- Display clear startup, connection, and packet transmission information.

The receiver should:
- Enable Wi-Fi CSI using the supported ESP-IDF APIs.
- Capture real CSI data and associated RSSI, timestamps, and packet metadata.
- Stream data over serial with a consistent, documented format.
- Avoid expensive processing inside the CSI callback.
- Report packet reception rates and errors.

Prefer the official Espressif CSI serial output format to minimize custom firmware changes.

Provide accurate macOS installation, build, and flashing instructions using ESP-IDF.

## 4. Python Backend

Create a local Python application with:

- Automatic detection or manual selection of serial ports.
- Reliable parsing of actual Espressif CSI output.
- Handling of malformed packets and disconnections.
- A bounded in-memory data buffer.
- Raw data recording and CSV export.
- Reconnect handling.
- Real-time packet rate and signal diagnostics.

Properly decode CSI complex values into per-subcarrier amplitudes, accounting for the actual CSI format and metadata.

Implement filtering and smoothing to reduce interference.

Analyze changes over time to calculate a **motion activity score**.

Initially use signal variance, baseline deviation, and temporal features rather than requiring a trained neural network.

No fabricated readings should appear in live hardware mode.

## 5. Live Dashboard

Use Streamlit or another lightweight local visualization framework.

Build a clean, modern dark-mode dashboard.

Display:

**A. Connection status**
- Transmitter/receiver configuration
- Serial connection status
- Incoming packet rate
- Signal quality indicators

**B. Live CSI visualization**
- Scrolling CSI subcarrier heatmap
- Signal amplitude over time
- Motion activity graph
- Baseline deviation

**C. Motion classification**
- Empty room / low activity
- Movement detected
- Rapid movement
- Potential fall
- Unknown / insufficient data

**D. Alerts**
- Visible potential-fall alert
- Countdown before a simulated caregiver notification
- Cancel alert button
- Event log

Never imply that prototype predictions are medically validated.

## 6. Self-Calibration

Add a guided calibration workflow.

Step 1: Record an empty, stationary room baseline for 15–30 seconds.

Step 2: Have the user walk across the sensing area.

Step 3: Record standing still and ordinary sitting.

Step 4: Determine initial signal variability, noise levels, and preliminary motion thresholds.

The dashboard should visualize the differences between the baseline and movement data.

Make recalibration easy.

Persist calibration parameters locally and associate them with the sensor configuration.

## 7. Labeled Data Collection

Create a recording interface with buttons for these labels:

- Empty room
- Standing still
- Walking
- Sitting
- Lying down
- Rapid sitting
- Simulated fall

Each recording must contain timestamps, CSI measurements, metadata, and the selected label.

Provide a way to replay recorded sessions through the same processing pipeline.

Organize recordings by session so that future machine learning evaluation can hold out complete sessions rather than randomly splitting individual packets.

## 8. Basic Fall Detection

Initially use an explainable, configurable heuristic:

1. Detect a sudden increase in motion activity.
2. Look for a substantial reduction in movement afterward.
3. Mark the event as a potential fall if both conditions occur within configurable time windows.
4. Require sufficient data quality before making a classification.

Show which criteria triggered the alert.

This is only a baseline. Do not assume low movement necessarily means a person is on the ground.

Add optional training code for a Random Forest classifier once labeled real data exists.

Do not claim accuracy without evaluating held-out real recordings.

## 9. Simulation Mode

Build a separate simulation mode that works without connecting an ESP32.

Generate plausible synthetic CSI-like movement patterns for:
- Empty room
- Walking
- Sitting
- Rapid movement
- Potential falls

Allow adjustable noise, motion strength, and event duration.

Simulated data must be clearly identified as synthetic and should never be used as evidence of real-world fall detection accuracy.

Use the same dashboard and detection pipeline for simulation and live data.

Provide a replay feature for real recorded CSI.

## 10. Project Structure and Documentation

Organize the project into:

- `firmware/transmitter/`
- `firmware/receiver/`
- `backend/`
- `dashboard/`
- `simulation/`
- `data/`
- `tests/`
- `README.md`

Adjust the structure if using official ESP-CSI examples without copying their entire repository.

Include:

- `requirements.txt` or `pyproject.toml`
- A one-command way to start the dashboard
- Setup instructions for macOS
- ESP32 flashing commands
- Serial device troubleshooting
- Basic unit tests for CSI parsing and motion detection

## 11. Execution Order

Work in this exact order:

**Milestone 1 — Working CSI connection**

Get real ESP32 CSI measurements into Python and print packet counts and amplitudes. This is the highest priority.

**Milestone 2 — Live dashboard**

Display actual CSI heatmaps and movement scores in real time.

**Milestone 3 — Calibration and recording**

Implement baseline calibration and labeled data collection.

**Milestone 4 — Fall detection**

Implement the initial heuristic classifier and test it with recorded examples.

**Milestone 5 — Simulation and presentation**

Add synthetic demonstrations, event replay, visual improvements, and export functionality.

Each milestone should produce an independently usable system.

If hardware is not connected, implement the software against the documented Espressif format and add fixtures and simulation support. Do not pretend hardware integration has been verified.

## 12. Acceptance Criteria

The minimum successful prototype must:

1. Run locally on my MacBook.
2. Receive and visualize actual CSI packets from two ESP32s.
3. Visibly react when someone moves between the ESP32s.
4. Support recording and replaying labeled motion data.
5. Offer empty-room baseline calibration.
6. Trigger an explainable potential-fall alert from configurable signal features.
7. Continue functioning without internet access.

**Begin implementing the project now, starting with the official ESP-CSI examples and the serial-to-Python processing pipeline. Prioritize a testable prototype over perfection. Do not stop after producing a plan.**

(Follow-up from user: "keep going")

- **`bash -n firmware/flash_helper.sh`:** passes. The script was never executed and no device was touched.

The firmware has not been compiled (ESP-IDF isn't installed) and nothing has been tested on hardware; the READMEs say so.

**What was built**
- **Firmware:** `firmware/transmitter` and `firmware/receiver` are standalone ESP-IDF projects taken from the official `csi_send` and `csi_recv` examples and changed as little as possible. Changes:
  - Channel and send rate are configurable; the transmitter prints a once-per-second `EG_TX_STATS` line.
  - The receiver's CSI callback now only copies the packet into a queue; a separate task prints the official `CSI_DATA` lines.
  - By default classic chips print only the first 128 values, so 100 Hz fits 921600 baud; the receiver prints a once-per-second `EG_RX_STATS` line.
  - An `sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag` file routes output to the native USB port (needed for the XIAO ESP32-S3).
  - `flash_helper.sh` requires an explicit port, runs a read-only chip check, checks the chip matches the target, and asks you to type the port name before flashing.
- **Backend:** `csi_parser.py`, `sources.py`, `ports.py`, `buffer.py`, `recorder.py`, `cli.py`.
- **Other files:** tests with fixtures (marked as format fixtures, not real captures), README.md, Makefile, pinned requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, .gitignore, and `data/*/.gitkeep`.
- **Git:** repo initialised with no commits; `git add -N .` has been run, and it includes `.agents/`.

**Things later features need to know**
- **Header name mismatch:** the official firmware's header says `rx_format`, while the official README and parser say `rx_state`. Our classic header prints `rx_state` with the real `rx_ctrl->rx_state` value (the official code printed `sig_mode` there twice). The parser accepts either header.
- **Fixtures:** both example lines in the official README turned out to be complete (128 and 256 values), so the fixtures use them verbatim.
- **Unverified field:** I assumed `rx_ctrl->rx_state` exists on classic targets based on the IDF headers, but couldn't compile to confirm.
- **Python stand-in:** miniconda Python 3.12 lacks streamlit, plotly and scikit-learn, so it can't replace `.venv` for FEAT-002.
- **Bug fixed:** the monitor printed in a tight loop once a replay ended while `--duration` was still running.

The full API summary, pins and deviation list are in the `findings` field of FEAT-001.json.

"""Parser for the official Espressif esp-csi ``CSI_DATA`` serial line format.

Two variants are printed by ``examples/get-started/csi_recv`` (and by the
EchoGuard receiver firmware, which keeps the same layout):

* classic ESP32 / ESP32-S3 / ESP32-C3, 25 comma separated fields::

    type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,
    aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,
    secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data

* ESP32-C5 / ESP32-C6 / ESP32-C61, 15 fields::

    type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,
    local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data

``data`` is a quoted JSON-style list of ``len`` signed integers, interleaved
``[imag0, real0, imag1, real1, ...]`` per subcarrier. The official parser
(``tools/csi_data_read_parse.py``) builds ``complex(raw[2k+1], raw[2k])``, i.e.
``real = raw[2k+1]`` and ``imag = raw[2k]``; this module does the same.

On classic chips the first 128 values are the LLTF (64 subcarriers) in the
order subcarrier 0..31 followed by -32..-1. Index 0 is DC; the 52 subcarriers
that carry legacy 20 MHz data/pilots are indices 1..26 and 38..63. When
``first_word`` (first_word_invalid) is 1 the first four bytes, i.e. subcarriers
0 and 1, are invalid and are masked as NaN.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np

CLASSIC_FIELDS = [
    "type", "id", "mac", "rssi", "rate", "sig_mode", "mcs", "bandwidth", "smoothing",
    "not_sounding", "aggregation", "stbc", "fec_coding", "sgi", "noise_floor", "ampdu_cnt",
    "channel", "secondary_channel", "local_timestamp", "ant", "sig_len", "rx_state", "len",
    "first_word", "data",
]
C5C6_FIELDS = [
    "type", "seq", "mac", "rssi", "rate", "noise_floor", "fft_gain", "agc_gain", "channel",
    "local_timestamp", "sig_len", "rx_state", "len", "first_word", "data",
]

CSI_TAG = "CSI_DATA"
FAMILY_CLASSIC = "classic"
FAMILY_C5C6 = "c5c6"

LLTF_SUBCARRIERS = 64
LLTF_VALUES = 2 * LLTF_SUBCARRIERS
#: LLTF subcarrier indices (0..63, order 0..31 then -32..-1) carrying legacy data/pilots.
VALID_LLTF_INDICES = np.array(list(range(1, 27)) + list(range(38, 64)), dtype=np.int64)

_ANSI_RE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[ -/]*[@-~]")
_MAC_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{2}(:[0-9a-fA-F]{2}){5}$")


class ParseError(ValueError):
    """A line that contains ``CSI_DATA`` but cannot be decoded.

    ``reason`` is a short machine readable code (``field_count``,
    ``non_numeric``, ``bad_mac``, ``bad_data``, ``truncated_data``,
    ``len_mismatch``, ``odd_value_count``, ``empty_data``).
    """

    def __init__(self, reason: str, detail: str, line: str = ""):
        super().__init__(f"{reason}: {detail}")
        self.reason = reason
        self.detail = detail
        self.line = line


@dataclass
class CSIPacket:
    """One decoded CSI measurement. Field names follow the official headers."""

    host_ts: Optional[float]
    chip_family: str
    seq: int                      # 'id' (classic) or 'seq' (C5/C6): TX packet counter
    mac: str
    rssi: int
    rate: int
    noise_floor: int
    channel: int
    local_timestamp: int          # receiver clock, microseconds
    sig_len: int
    rx_state: int
    len: int                      # number of int values in 'data'
    first_word_invalid: bool
    raw: list
    csi: np.ndarray               # complex64, one value per subcarrier
    amplitude: np.ndarray         # float32 |csi|
    phase: np.ndarray             # float32 angle(csi), radians
    raw_line: str
    # classic-only header fields (None on C5/C6)
    sig_mode: Optional[int] = None
    mcs: Optional[int] = None
    bandwidth: Optional[int] = None
    smoothing: Optional[int] = None
    not_sounding: Optional[int] = None
    aggregation: Optional[int] = None
    stbc: Optional[int] = None
    fec_coding: Optional[int] = None
    sgi: Optional[int] = None
    ampdu_cnt: Optional[int] = None
    secondary_channel: Optional[int] = None
    ant: Optional[int] = None
    # C5/C6-only header fields (None on classic)
    fft_gain: Optional[int] = None
    agc_gain: Optional[int] = None

    @property
    def n_subcarriers(self) -> int:
        return int(self.csi.shape[0])


@dataclass
class RxStats:
    """``EG_RX_STATS`` line printed once per second by the EchoGuard receiver."""

    uptime_ms: int
    csi_rx_total: int
    csi_rx_rate_hz: float
    queue_drops: int
    seq_gaps: int
    last_rssi: int
    host_ts: Optional[float] = None


@dataclass
class TxStats:
    """``EG_TX_STATS`` line printed once per second by the EchoGuard transmitter."""

    uptime_ms: int
    sent_ok: int
    send_fail: int
    rate_hz: float
    host_ts: Optional[float] = None


@dataclass
class ParsedLine:
    """Result of :func:`parse_any`. ``kind`` is csi|malformed|stats|header|other|empty."""

    kind: str
    line: str
    packet: Optional[CSIPacket] = None
    error: Optional[ParseError] = None
    stats: Optional[object] = None
    header_family: Optional[str] = None
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


def clean_line(line) -> str:
    """Decode bytes, strip ANSI colour codes, CR/LF and surrounding whitespace."""
    if isinstance(line, (bytes, bytearray)):
        line = line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    line = _ANSI_RE.sub("", line)
    return line.strip().strip("\x00")


def header_family(line: str) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return 'classic' / 'c5c6' if ``line`` is an official CSV header line."""
    s = clean_line(line)
    if s.startswith("type,id,mac,") and s.count(",") == len(CLASSIC_FIELDS) - 1:
        return FAMILY_CLASSIC
    if s.startswith("type,seq,mac,") and s.count(",") == len(C5C6_FIELDS) - 1:
        return FAMILY_C5C6
    return None


def _to_int(name: str, value: str, line: str) -> int:
    try:
        return int(value.strip())
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        raise ParseError("non_numeric", f"field '{name}' is not an integer: {value!r}", line) from None


def _parse_data(text: str, line: str) -> list:
    s = text.strip()
    if not s.startswith("["):
        raise ParseError("bad_data", "data field does not start with '['", line)
    if not s.endswith("]"):
        raise ParseError("truncated_data", "data array is not terminated with ']'", line)
    body = s[1:-1].strip()
    if not body:
        raise ParseError("empty_data", "data array is empty", line)
    try:
        return [int(v) for v in body.split(",")]
    except ValueError:
        raise ParseError("bad_data", "data array contains non-integer values", line) from None


def decode_complex(raw) -> np.ndarray:
    """Interleaved [imag, real, ...] ints -> complex array (real=raw[2k+1], imag=raw[2k])."""
    arr = np.asarray(raw, dtype=np.float32)
    if arr.size % 2:
        raise ValueError("odd number of CSI values")
    return (arr[1::2] + 1j * arr[0::2]).astype(np.complex64)


def parse_line(line, host_ts: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[CSIPacket]:
    """Parse one serial line.

    Returns ``None`` for lines that are not CSI data (logs, headers, stats).
    Raises :class:`ParseError` for lines that contain ``CSI_DATA`` but are
    malformed. ESP log prefixes, ANSI codes and CRLF are tolerated.
    """
    s = clean_line(line)
    idx = s.find(CSI_TAG)
    if idx < 0:
        return None
    s = s[idx:]

    try:
        fields = next(csv.reader([s]))
    except csv.Error as e:
        raise ParseError("bad_data", f"csv error: {e}", s) from None
    n = len(fields)
    if n == len(CLASSIC_FIELDS):
        family, names = FAMILY_CLASSIC, CLASSIC_FIELDS
    elif n == len(C5C6_FIELDS):
        family, names = FAMILY_C5C6, C5C6_FIELDS
    else:
        raise ParseError(
            "field_count",
            f"{n} fields (expected {len(CLASSIC_FIELDS)} classic or {len(C5C6_FIELDS)} C5/C6)",
            s,
        )
    if fields[0] != CSI_TAG:
        raise ParseError("bad_data", f"unexpected type field {fields[0]!r}", s)

    rec = dict(zip(names, fields))
    mac = rec["mac"].strip().lower()
    if not _MAC_RE.match(mac):
        raise ParseError("bad_mac", f"invalid MAC {rec['mac']!r}", s)

    ints = {k: _to_int(k, rec[k], s) for k in names if k not in ("type", "mac", "data")}
    raw = _parse_data(rec["data"], s)
    if ints["len"] != len(raw):
        raise ParseError("len_mismatch", f"len field {ints['len']} != {len(raw)} values", s)
    if len(raw) % 2:
        raise ParseError("odd_value_count", f"{len(raw)} values is not a whole number of subcarriers", s)

    csi = decode_complex(raw)
    seq = ints["id"] if family == FAMILY_CLASSIC else ints["seq"]
    pkt = CSIPacket(
        host_ts=host_ts,
        chip_family=family,
        seq=seq,
        mac=mac,
        rssi=ints["rssi"],
        rate=ints["rate"],
        noise_floor=ints["noise_floor"],
        channel=ints["channel"],
        local_timestamp=ints["local_timestamp"],
        sig_len=ints["sig_len"],
        rx_state=ints["rx_state"],
        len=ints["len"],
        first_word_invalid=bool(ints["first_word"]),
        raw=raw,
        csi=csi,
        amplitude=np.abs(csi).astype(np.float32),
        phase=np.angle(csi).astype(np.float32),
        raw_line=s,
    )
    if family == FAMILY_CLASSIC:
        for k in ("sig_mode", "mcs", "bandwidth", "smoothing", "not_sounding", "aggregation", "stbc",
                  "fec_coding", "sgi", "ampdu_cnt", "secondary_channel", "ant"):
            setattr(pkt, k, ints[k])
    else:
        pkt.fft_gain = ints["fft_gain"]
        pkt.agc_gain = ints["agc_gain"]
    return pkt


def _masked_amplitudes(pkt: CSIPacket) -> np.ndarray:
    amp = pkt.amplitude.astype(np.float64)
    if pkt.first_word_invalid and amp.size:
        amp[: min(2, amp.size)] = np.nan
    return amp


def lltf_amplitudes(pkt: CSIPacket) -> np.ndarray:
    """64 LLTF subcarrier amplitudes (order 0..31, -32..-1) for classic chips.

    Subcarriers 0 and 1 are NaN when ``first_word_invalid``. Missing values (a
    packet shorter than 128 values) are NaN. Raises ``ValueError`` for C5/C6
    packets, whose layout does not start with an LLTF block.
    """
    if pkt.chip_family != FAMILY_CLASSIC:
        raise ValueError("LLTF layout is only defined for classic ESP32/S3/C3 packets")
    out = np.full(LLTF_SUBCARRIERS, np.nan)
    amp = _masked_amplitudes(pkt)[:LLTF_SUBCARRIERS]
    out[: amp.size] = amp
    return out


def valid_subcarrier_amplitudes(pkt: CSIPacket) -> np.ndarray:
    """Amplitudes of the subcarriers that carry signal.

    Classic: the 52 legacy LLTF subcarriers (``VALID_LLTF_INDICES``); index 1 is
    NaN when ``first_word_invalid``. C5/C6: all subcarriers (with the first two
    NaN when ``first_word_invalid``); downstream code should drop columns that
    are constantly zero (guard/null subcarriers), since the C5/C6 layout depends
    on the received PPDU format and is not fixed here.
    """
    if pkt.chip_family == FAMILY_CLASSIC:
        return lltf_amplitudes(pkt)[VALID_LLTF_INDICES]
    return _masked_amplitudes(pkt)


def subcarrier_labels(pkt: CSIPacket) -> list:
    """Column labels matching :func:`valid_subcarrier_amplitudes`."""
    if pkt.chip_family == FAMILY_CLASSIC:
        return [f"lltf_{i}" for i in VALID_LLTF_INDICES]
    return [f"sc_{i}" for i in range(pkt.n_subcarriers)]


def parse_stats_line(line, host_ts: Optional[float] = None):
    """Parse ``EG_RX_STATS`` / ``EG_TX_STATS`` lines. Returns None for other lines."""
    s = clean_line(line)
    for tag, n_fields in (("EG_RX_STATS", 7), ("EG_TX_STATS", 5)):
        idx = s.find(tag)
        if idx < 0:
            continue
        parts = s[idx:].split(",")
        if len(parts) != n_fields:
            return None
        try:
            if tag == "EG_RX_STATS":
                return RxStats(int(parts[1]), int(parts[2]), float(parts[3]), int(parts[4]),
                               int(parts[5]), int(parts[6]), host_ts)
            return TxStats(int(parts[1]), int(parts[2]), int(parts[3]), float(parts[4]), host_ts)
        except ValueError:
            return None
    return None


def parse_any(line, host_ts: Optional[float] = None) -> ParsedLine:
    """Classify and parse any serial line without raising."""
    s = clean_line(line)
    if not s:
        return ParsedLine("empty", s)
    if CSI_TAG in s:
        try:
            return ParsedLine("csi", s, packet=parse_line(s, host_ts))
        except ParseError as e:
            return ParsedLine("malformed", s, error=e)
    fam = header_family(s)
    if fam:
        return ParsedLine("header", s, header_family=fam)
    stats = parse_stats_line(s, host_ts)
    if stats is not None:
        return ParsedLine("stats", s, stats=stats)
    return ParsedLine("other", s)

"""Line sources: live serial, and replay of recordings / raw serial logs.

Every source yields ``(host_ts, line)`` tuples of raw text so live data,
replays (and, later, simulation) all go through the same parser and pipeline.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import threading
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Iterator, Optional, Tuple

from .recorder import RAW_FIELDS

Line = Tuple[float, str]

# Upper bound for a partial line kept between reads (a full HT40 CSI line is < 4 kB).
_MAX_PENDING = 64 * 1024


@dataclass
class SourceStatus:
    kind: str
    port: str = ""
    connected: bool = False
    finished: bool = False
    reconnect_count: int = 0
    last_error: str = ""
    bytes_read: int = 0
    lines_read: int = 0
    connected_since: Optional[float] = None
    extra: dict = field(default_factory=dict)


class LineSource:
    """Base class. Iterate :meth:`lines`; call :meth:`stop` from another thread."""

    kind = "base"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._stop = threading.Event()
        self.status = SourceStatus(kind=self.kind)

    def lines(self) -> Iterator[Line]:  # pragma: no cover - interface
        raise NotImplementedError

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self._stop.set()

    @property
    def stopped(self) -> bool:
        return self._stop.is_set()

    def __iter__(self):
        return self.lines()


class SerialSource(LineSource):
    """Read lines from an ESP32 over USB serial with automatic reconnect.

    ``port`` may be a device path, a pyserial URL (``loop://`` for tests) or
    ``"auto"``, which is resolved via :func:`backend.ports.auto_select` on every
    (re)connect so a re-enumerated board is found again.
    """

    kind = "serial"

    def __init__(
        self,
        port: str,
        baud: int = 921600,
        read_timeout: float = 0.2,
        backoff_initial: float = 0.5,
        backoff_max: float = 5.0,
        serial_factory: Optional[Callable[[str, int, float], object]] = None,
        port_resolver: Optional[Callable[[], str]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.port = port
        self.baud = baud
        self.read_timeout = read_timeout
        self.backoff_initial = backoff_initial
        self.backoff_max = backoff_max
        self._factory = serial_factory or self._default_factory
        self._resolver = port_resolver
        self._ser = None
        self.status.port = port

    @staticmethod
    def _default_factory(port: str, baud: int, timeout: float):
        import serial

        return serial.serial_for_url(port, baudrate=baud, timeout=timeout)

    def _resolve_port(self) -> str:
        if self.port != "auto":
            return self.port
        if self._resolver is not None:
            return self._resolver()
        from .ports import auto_select, probe_port

        return auto_select(probe=lambda dev: probe_port(dev, baud=self.baud))

    def _open(self) -> bool:
        try:
            device = self._resolve_port()
            self._ser = self._factory(device, self.baud, self.read_timeout)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - SerialException, OSError, PortSelectionError
            self._ser = None
            self.status.connected = False
            self.status.last_error = str(e)
            return False
        self.status.port = device
        self.status.connected = True
        self.status.connected_since = time.time()
        self.status.last_error = ""
        return True

    def _close(self) -> None:
        ser, self._ser = self._ser, None
        self.status.connected = False
        if ser is not None:
            try:
                ser.close()
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
                pass

    def lines(self) -> Iterator[Line]:
        backoff = self.backoff_initial
        pending = b""
        ever_connected = False
        try:
            while not self._stop.is_set():
                if self._ser is None:
                    if not self._open():
                        self._stop.wait(backoff)
                        backoff = min(backoff * 2, self.backoff_max)
                        continue
                    if ever_connected:
                        self.status.reconnect_count += 1
                    ever_connected = True
                    backoff = self.backoff_initial
                    pending = b""
                try:
                    chunk = self._ser.readline()
                except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - SerialException / OSError on unplug
                    self.status.last_error = f"disconnected: {e}"
                    self._close()
                    continue
                if not chunk:
                    continue
                self.status.bytes_read += len(chunk)
                pending += chunk
                if not pending.endswith(b"\n"):
                    # readline() timed out mid-line; keep the fragment.
                    if len(pending) > _MAX_PENDING:
                        pending = b""
                    continue
                text = pending.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip("\r\n")
                pending = b""
                self.status.lines_read += 1
                yield time.time(), text
        finally:
            self._close()


class ReplaySource(LineSource):
    """Re-emit recorded lines through the normal pipeline.

    Accepts two formats:

    * EchoGuard recordings written by :class:`backend.recorder.RawRecorder`
      (CSV with ``host_ts_iso,host_ts_unix,raw_line,...``): original relative
      timing is reproduced, scaled by ``speed``.
    * plain raw serial logs (``.txt`` / ``.log``, e.g. ``idf.py monitor``
      captures, test fixtures): no host timestamps exist, so lines are emitted
      at ``line_rate_hz`` (scaled by ``speed``).

    ``speed=0`` means as fast as possible. Yielded ``host_ts`` values follow
    the (scaled) original timeline starting at the replay start time, so rate
    calculations stay meaningful.
    """

    kind = "replay"

    def __init__(self, path, speed: float = 1.0, loop: bool = False, line_rate_hz: float = 100.0) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.speed = float(speed)
        self.loop = loop
        self.line_rate_hz = float(line_rate_hz)
        self.status.port = str(self.path)
        self.recording_format = self._detect_format()
        self.status.extra["format"] = self.recording_format

    def _detect_format(self) -> str:
        with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as f:
            first = f.readline()
        return "recording" if first.startswith(",".join(RAW_FIELDS)) else "raw_log"

    def _iter_original(self) -> Iterator[Tuple[float, str]]:
        """Yield (original_relative_seconds, line)."""
        if self.recording_format == "recording":
            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace", newline="") as f:
                t0 = None
                for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                    try:
                        ts = float(row["host_ts_unix"])
                    except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError):
                        continue
                    if t0 is None:
                        t0 = ts
                    yield ts - t0, row.get("raw_line") or ""
        else:
            period = 1.0 / self.line_rate_hz if self.line_rate_hz > 0 else 0.0
            with open(self.path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
                for i, line in enumerate(f):
                    yield i * period, line.rstrip("\r\n")

    def lines(self) -> Iterator[Line]:
        self.status.connected = True
        self.status.connected_since = time.time()
        start = time.time()
        loop_offset = 0.0
        try:
            while not self._stop.is_set():
                last_rel = 0.0
                for rel, line in self._iter_original():
                    if self._stop.is_set():
                        return
                    rel_scaled = (rel / self.speed) if self.speed > 0 else rel
                    last_rel = rel_scaled
                    target = start + loop_offset + rel_scaled
                    if self.speed > 0:
                        delay = target - time.time()
                        if delay > 0 and self._stop.wait(delay):
                            return
                    self.status.lines_read += 1
                    self.status.bytes_read += len(line) + 1
                    yield target, line
                if not self.loop:
                    break
                gap = (1.0 / self.line_rate_hz) if self.line_rate_hz > 0 else 0.01
                loop_offset += last_rel + gap
        finally:
            self.status.connected = False
            self.status.finished = True

"""Thread-safe bounded CSI packet buffer with live link diagnostics."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import threading
from collections import Counter, deque
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

from .csi_parser import CSIPacket, ParsedLine, RxStats, TxStats, parse_any

SEQ_MOD = 2 ** 32
#: A forward jump larger than this is treated as a transmitter restart, not loss.
MAX_PLAUSIBLE_GAP = 10_000


@dataclass
class BufferStats:
    total_lines: int = 0
    csi_packets: int = 0
    malformed: int = 0
    malformed_reasons: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    non_csi_lines: int = 0
    header_family: Optional[str] = None
    seq_gaps: int = 0
    seq_resets: int = 0
    duplicates: int = 0
    packet_rate_hz: Optional[float] = None
    last_rssi: Optional[int] = None
    rssi_mean: Optional[float] = None
    rssi_std: Optional[float] = None
    noise_floor: Optional[int] = None
    last_len: Optional[int] = None
    chip_family: Optional[str] = None
    last_packet_ts: Optional[float] = None
    buffered: int = 0
    last_rx_stats: Optional[RxStats] = None
    last_tx_stats: Optional[TxStats] = None


class CSIBuffer:
    """Bounded ring buffer of :class:`CSIPacket` plus counters.

    Feed raw lines with :meth:`ingest` (parses them) or already parsed packets
    with :meth:`add_packet`. Safe to call from a reader thread while another
    thread reads :meth:`snapshot` / :meth:`packets`.
    """

    def __init__(self, maxlen: int = 3000, rate_window_s: float = 2.0, rssi_window: int = 200) -> None:
        self.maxlen = maxlen
        self.rate_window_s = rate_window_s
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._packets: deque = deque(maxlen=maxlen)
        self._rate_ts: deque = deque()
        self._rssi: deque = deque(maxlen=rssi_window)
        self._reasons: Counter = Counter()
        self._first_packet_ts: Optional[float] = None
        self._last_seq: Optional[int] = None
        self._s = BufferStats()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ input
    def ingest(self, host_ts: float, line: str) -> ParsedLine:
        parsed = parse_any(line, host_ts)
        with self._lock:
            self._s.total_lines += 1
            if parsed.kind == "csi":
                self._add_locked(parsed.packet)
            elif parsed.kind == "malformed":
                self._s.malformed += 1
                self._reasons[parsed.error.reason] += 1
            elif parsed.kind != "empty":
                self._s.non_csi_lines += 1
                if parsed.kind == "header":
                    self._s.header_family = parsed.header_family
                elif parsed.kind == "stats":
                    if isinstance(parsed.stats, RxStats):
                        self._s.last_rx_stats = parsed.stats
                    else:
                        self._s.last_tx_stats = parsed.stats
        return parsed

    def add_packet(self, pkt: CSIPacket) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._s.total_lines += 1
            self._add_locked(pkt)

    def _add_locked(self, pkt: CSIPacket) -> None:
        s = self._s
        s.csi_packets += 1
        self._packets.append(pkt)
        ts = pkt.host_ts
        if ts is not None:
            if self._first_packet_ts is None:
                self._first_packet_ts = ts
            s.last_packet_ts = ts
            self._rate_ts.append(ts)
            self._trim_rate(ts)
        self._update_seq(pkt.seq)
        s.last_rssi = pkt.rssi
        self._rssi.append(pkt.rssi)
        s.noise_floor = pkt.noise_floor
        s.last_len = pkt.len
        s.chip_family = pkt.chip_family

    def _update_seq(self, seq: int) -> None:
        last = self._last_seq
        self._last_seq = seq
        if last is None:
            return
        diff = (seq - last) % SEQ_MOD
        if diff == 1:
            return
        if diff == 0:
            self._s.duplicates += 1
        elif diff <= MAX_PLAUSIBLE_GAP:
            self._s.seq_gaps += diff - 1
        else:
            # backwards or huge jump: transmitter restarted, resynchronise
            self._s.seq_resets += 1

    def _trim_rate(self, now: float) -> None:
        cutoff = now - self.rate_window_s
        while self._rate_ts and self._rate_ts[0] <= cutoff:
            self._rate_ts.popleft()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- output
    def packet_rate(self, now: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[float]:
        with self._lock:
            return self._rate_locked(now)

    def _rate_locked(self, now: Optional[float]) -> Optional[float]:
        if self._first_packet_ts is None:
            return None
        if now is None:
            now = self._s.last_packet_ts
        self._trim_rate(now)
        span = min(self.rate_window_s, now - self._first_packet_ts)
        if span <= 0:
            return None
        n = sum(1 for t in self._rate_ts if t <= now)
        return n / span

    def snapshot(self, now: Optional[float] = None) -> BufferStats:
        """Copy of the current counters. ``now`` (host time) lets the rate decay to
        zero when packets stop; default is the last packet timestamp."""
        with self._lock:
            s = self._s
            out = BufferStats(**{k: getattr(s, k) for k in s.__dataclass_fields__})
            out.malformed_reasons = dict(self._reasons)
            out.packet_rate_hz = self._rate_locked(now)
            out.buffered = len(self._packets)
            if self._rssi:
                vals = list(self._rssi)
                mean = sum(vals) / len(vals)
                out.rssi_mean = mean
                out.rssi_std = math.sqrt(sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in vals) / len(vals))
            return out

    def packets(self, last_n: Optional[int] = None) -> list:
        with self._lock:
            if last_n is None or last_n >= len(self._packets):
                return list(self._packets)
            return list(self._packets)[-last_n:]

    def latest(self) -> Optional[CSIPacket]:
        with self._lock:
            return self._packets[-1] if self._packets else None

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        with self._lock:
            return len(self._packets)

/*

 */
/* EchoGuard CSI receiver

   Derived from espressif/esp-csi examples/get-started/csi_recv (Public Domain /
   CC0 example code). Kept unchanged: wifi_init(), ESP-NOW init, per-target
   csi_config, sender MAC filter, esp_csi_gain_ctrl logic, and the official
   CSI_DATA serial line formats (classic 25-field and C5/C6 15-field).

   EchoGuard changes:
     (a) No printing inside the CSI callback. The callback only copies rx_ctrl,
         mac, id, first_word_invalid, len, compensate_gain and up to
         ECHOGUARD_RX_MAX_CSI_BYTES of info->buf into a pre-allocated queue item
         and calls xQueueSend(..., 0). If the queue is full the packet is
         dropped and counted. A separate printer task formats the line.
     (b) The per-packet ESP_LOGI("compensate_gain ...") of the official
         callback is removed (it alone would flood the serial link).
     (c) ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY (default y, classic targets only) prints only
         the first 128 values (64 LLTF subcarriers) and sets 'len' accordingly.
     (d) Classic line: the 'rx_state' column prints rx_ctrl->rx_state (the
         official code passes sig_mode a second time there).
     (e) Once per second: EG_RX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<csi_rx_total>,
         <csi_rx_rate_hz>,<queue_drops>,<seq_gaps>,<last_rssi>
     (f) Startup banner (target, channel, expected TX MAC, LLTF-only flag).
     Channel comes from Kconfig ECHOGUARD_RX_CHANNEL (must match transmitter).

   Serial bandwidth (921600 baud UART, 8N1 = 92160 bytes/s):
     One CSI value prints as up to 4 chars plus a comma (e.g. "-12,"), on
     average ~3.5-4 bytes. Metadata prefix is ~100 bytes.
       LLTF only : 128 values * ~4 B + ~100 B  ~=  600 B/line
                   * 100 Hz                    ~=   60 kB/s  -> fits (~65 %)
       HT40 full : 384 values * ~4 B + ~100 B  ~= 1640 B/line
                   * 100 Hz                    ~=  164 kB/s  -> does NOT fit
     Hence LLTF-only is the default on classic targets.

   Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, this
   software is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR
   CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
*/

#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdarg.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <inttypes.h>

#include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h"
#include "freertos/task.h"
#include "freertos/queue.h"

#include "nvs_flash.h"

#include "esp_mac.h"
#include "rom/ets_sys.h"
#include "esp_log.h"
#include "esp_wifi.h"
#include "esp_netif.h"
#include "esp_now.h"
#include "esp_timer.h"
#include "esp_idf_version.h"
#include "esp_csi_gain_ctrl.h"

#define CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL   CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_CHANNEL

/* HT40 needs the secondary 20 MHz channel inside 1..13: "below" for 5..13
 * (official default for channel 11), "above" for 1..4. Same rule as the TX. */
#define EG_SECOND_CHAN ((CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL >= 5) ? WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_BELOW : WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_ABOVE)

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61 || (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 && ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(5, 4, 0))
#define CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE               WIFI_BAND_MODE_2G_ONLY
#define CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS           WIFI_BW_HT40
#define CONFIG_WIFI_5G_BANDWIDTHS           WIFI_BW_HT40
#define CONFIG_WIFI_2G_PROTOCOL             WIFI_PROTOCOL_11N
#define CONFIG_WIFI_5G_PROTOCOL             WIFI_PROTOCOL_11N
#else
#define CONFIG_WIFI_BANDWIDTH           WIFI_BW_HT40
#endif

#define CONFIG_ESP_NOW_PHYMODE           WIFI_PHY_MODE_HT40
#define CONFIG_ESP_NOW_RATE             WIFI_PHY_RATE_MCS0_LGI
#define CONFIG_FORCE_GAIN                   0

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
#define CSI_FORCE_LLTF                      0
#endif

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32S3 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C3 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
#define CONFIG_GAIN_CONTROL                 1
#endif

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
#define EG_C5C6_FORMAT                      1
#else
#define EG_C5C6_FORMAT                      0
#endif

#if ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(6, 0, 0)
#define ESP_IF_WIFI_STA ESP_MAC_WIFI_STA
#endif

/* Number of int8 values printed per packet at most. */
#if CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY
#define EG_LLTF_VALUES                      128
#define EG_COPY_MAX                         ((CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_MAX_CSI_BYTES < EG_LLTF_VALUES) ? CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_MAX_CSI_BYTES : EG_LLTF_VALUES)
#else
#define EG_COPY_MAX                         CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_MAX_CSI_BYTES
#endif

/* Worst case line: ~200 bytes metadata + 6 bytes per value ("-1234,"). */
#define EG_LINE_BUF_SIZE                    (256 + 6 * EG_COPY_MAX)

static const uint8_t CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC[] = {0x1a, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00};
static const char *TAG = "csi_recv";

/* One CSI packet as handed from the Wi-Fi callback to the printer task. */
typedef struct {
    wifi_pkt_rx_ctrl_t rx_ctrl;   /* full copy: cheap, avoids per-target field lists */
    uint8_t mac[6];
    uint32_t rx_id;
    float compensate_gain;
    uint8_t agc_gain;
    int8_t fft_gain;
    bool first_word_invalid;
    uint16_t len;                 /* number of bytes copied into buf */
    int8_t buf[EG_COPY_MAX];
} eg_csi_item_t;

static QueueHandle_t s_csi_queue = NULL;
/* The CSI callback runs in the Wi-Fi task only, so a single static staging item
 * is safe and keeps the large struct off the Wi-Fi task stack. */
static eg_csi_item_t s_cb_item;
static eg_csi_item_t s_print_item;
static char s_line[EG_LINE_BUF_SIZE];

/* Counters updated in the callback (single writer), read by the printer task. */
static volatile uint32_t s_rx_total = 0;
static volatile uint32_t s_queue_drops = 0;
static volatile uint32_t s_seq_gaps = 0;
static volatile int32_t s_last_rssi = 0;

static void wifi_init()
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_event_loop_create_default());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_netif_init());
    wifi_init_config_t cfg = WIFI_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_init(&cfg));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_STA));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_storage(WIFI_STORAGE_RAM));

#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());
    esp_wifi_set_band_mode(CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE);
    wifi_protocols_t protocols = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_PROTOCOL,
        .ghz_5g = CONFIG_WIFI_5G_PROTOCOL
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_protocols(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &protocols));
    wifi_bandwidths_t bandwidth = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS,
        .ghz_5g = CONFIG_WIFI_5G_BANDWIDTHS
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_bandwidths(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &bandwidth));
#elif (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 && ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(5, 4, 0)) || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());
    esp_wifi_set_band_mode(CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE);
    wifi_protocols_t protocols = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_PROTOCOL,
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_protocols(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &protocols));
    wifi_bandwidths_t bandwidth = {
        .ghz_2g = CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS,
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_bandwidths(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, &bandwidth));
#else
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_bandwidth(ESP_IF_WIFI_STA, CONFIG_WIFI_BANDWIDTH));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_start());
#endif

    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_ps(WIFI_PS_NONE));
#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5
    if ((CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE == WIFI_BAND_MODE_2G_ONLY && CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS == WIFI_BW_HT20)
            || (CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE == WIFI_BAND_MODE_5G_ONLY && CONFIG_WIFI_5G_BANDWIDTHS == WIFI_BW_HT20)) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE));
    } else {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, EG_SECOND_CHAN));
    }
#elif (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6 && ESP_IDF_VERSION >= ESP_IDF_VERSION_VAL(5, 4, 0)) || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    if (CONFIG_WIFI_BAND_MODE == WIFI_BAND_MODE_2G_ONLY && CONFIG_WIFI_2G_BANDWIDTHS == WIFI_BW_HT20) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE));
    } else {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, EG_SECOND_CHAN));
    }
#else
    if (CONFIG_WIFI_BANDWIDTH == WIFI_BW_HT20) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_NONE));
    } else {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_channel(CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL, EG_SECOND_CHAN));
    }
#endif

    /* Official example behaviour, kept unchanged. */
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_mac(WIFI_IF_STA, CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC));
}

static void wifi_esp_now_init(esp_now_peer_info_t peer)
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_init());
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_set_pmk((uint8_t *)"pmk1234567890123"));
    esp_now_rate_config_t rate_config = {
        .phymode = CONFIG_ESP_NOW_PHYMODE,
        .rate = CONFIG_ESP_NOW_RATE,//  WIFI_PHY_RATE_MCS0_LGI,
        .ersu = false,
        .dcm = false
    };
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_add_peer(&peer));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_now_set_peer_rate_config(peer.peer_addr, &rate_config));

}

/* Runs in the Wi-Fi task. Keep it short: copy, enqueue, count. */
static void wifi_csi_rx_cb(void *ctx, wifi_csi_info_t *info)
{
    if (!info || !info->buf) {
        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "<%s> wifi_csi_cb", esp_err_to_name(ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG));
        return;
    }

    if (memcmp(info->mac, CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC, 6)) {
        return;
    }

    const wifi_pkt_rx_ctrl_t *rx_ctrl = &info->rx_ctrl;
    static uint32_t s_count = 0;
    float compensate_gain = 1.0f;
    static uint8_t agc_gain = 0;
    static int8_t fft_gain = 0;
#if CONFIG_GAIN_CONTROL
    static uint8_t agc_gain_baseline = 0;
    static int8_t fft_gain_baseline = 0;
    esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_rx_gain(rx_ctrl, &agc_gain, &fft_gain);
    if (s_count < 100) {
        esp_csi_gain_ctrl_record_rx_gain(agc_gain, fft_gain);
    } else if (s_count == 100) {
        esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_rx_gain_baseline(&agc_gain_baseline, &fft_gain_baseline);
#if CONFIG_FORCE_GAIN
        esp_csi_gain_ctrl_set_rx_force_gain(agc_gain_baseline, fft_gain_baseline);
        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "fft_force %d, agc_force %d", fft_gain_baseline, agc_gain_baseline);
#endif
    }
    esp_csi_gain_ctrl_get_gain_compensation(&compensate_gain, agc_gain, fft_gain);
    /* (b) official per-packet ESP_LOGI of compensate_gain removed. */
#endif

    const uint32_t rx_id = *(uint32_t *)(info->payload + 15);

    /* Sequence gap accounting: the TX payload is a +1 counter. A smaller id
     * means the transmitter rebooted; resynchronise without counting a gap. */
    static bool s_have_last_id = false;
    static uint32_t s_last_id = 0;
    if (s_have_last_id && rx_id > s_last_id + 1) {
        s_seq_gaps += rx_id - s_last_id - 1;
    }
    s_last_id = rx_id;
    s_have_last_id = true;

    s_rx_total++;
    s_last_rssi = rx_ctrl->rssi;
    s_count++;

    eg_csi_item_t *item = &s_cb_item;
    memcpy(&item->rx_ctrl, rx_ctrl, sizeof(wifi_pkt_rx_ctrl_t));
    memcpy(item->mac, info->mac, 6);
    item->rx_id = rx_id;
    item->compensate_gain = compensate_gain;
    item->agc_gain = agc_gain;
    item->fft_gain = fft_gain;
    item->first_word_invalid = info->first_word_invalid;
    uint16_t n = info->len;
    if (n > EG_COPY_MAX) {
        n = EG_COPY_MAX;
    }
    item->len = n;
    memcpy(item->buf, info->buf, n);

    if (xQueueSend(s_csi_queue, item, 0) != pdTRUE) {
        s_queue_drops++;
    }
}

/* Append printf-style text to s_line, never overflowing. */
static size_t line_appendf(size_t pos, const char *fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
static size_t line_appendf(size_t pos, const char *fmt, ...)
{
    if (pos >= sizeof(s_line)) {
        return pos;
    }
    va_list ap;
    va_start(ap, fmt);
    int w = vsnprintf(s_line + pos, sizeof(s_line) - pos, fmt, ap);
    va_end(ap);
    if (w < 0) {
        return pos;
    }
    pos += (size_t)w;
    return (pos < sizeof(s_line)) ? pos : sizeof(s_line) - 1;
}

static void print_csi_item(const eg_csi_item_t *it)
{
    const wifi_pkt_rx_ctrl_t *rx_ctrl = &it->rx_ctrl;
    size_t pos = 0;

#if EG_C5C6_FORMAT
    /* Official C5/C6 layout. The 'rx_state' / 'rx_format' column carries
     * cur_bb_format exactly as in the official example (kept: these targets
     * report the baseband format here and the official tools expect it). */
    pos = line_appendf(pos, "CSI_DATA,%" PRIu32 "," MACSTR ",%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%u,%d,%d",
                       it->rx_id, MAC2STR(it->mac), (int)rx_ctrl->rssi, (int)rx_ctrl->rate,
                       (int)rx_ctrl->noise_floor, (int)it->fft_gain, (int)it->agc_gain, (int)rx_ctrl->channel,
                       (unsigned)rx_ctrl->timestamp, (int)rx_ctrl->sig_len, (int)rx_ctrl->cur_bb_format);
#else
    /* Official classic layout; (d) rx_state column now prints rx_ctrl->rx_state. */
    pos = line_appendf(pos, "CSI_DATA,%" PRIu32 "," MACSTR ",%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%u,%d,%d,%d",
                       it->rx_id, MAC2STR(it->mac), (int)rx_ctrl->rssi, (int)rx_ctrl->rate, (int)rx_ctrl->sig_mode,
                       (int)rx_ctrl->mcs, (int)rx_ctrl->cwb, (int)rx_ctrl->smoothing, (int)rx_ctrl->not_sounding,
                       (int)rx_ctrl->aggregation, (int)rx_ctrl->stbc, (int)rx_ctrl->fec_coding, (int)rx_ctrl->sgi,
                       (int)rx_ctrl->noise_floor, (int)rx_ctrl->ampdu_cnt, (int)rx_ctrl->channel, (int)rx_ctrl->secondary_channel,
                       (unsigned)rx_ctrl->timestamp, (int)rx_ctrl->ant, (int)rx_ctrl->sig_len, (int)rx_ctrl->rx_state);
#endif

    const float g = it->compensate_gain;
#if (CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61) && CSI_FORCE_LLTF
    /* Official 12-bit packed LLTF decoding for C5/C61 with force-LLTF. */
    const int n = (it->len >= 2) ? it->len : 2;
    int16_t csi = ((int16_t)(((((uint16_t)(uint8_t)it->buf[1]) << 8) | (uint8_t)it->buf[0]) << 4) >> 4);
    pos = line_appendf(pos, ",%d,%d,\"[%d", (n - 2) / 2, it->first_word_invalid, (int16_t)(g * csi));
    for (int i = 2; i < (n - 2); i += 2) {
        csi = ((int16_t)(((((uint16_t)(uint8_t)it->buf[i + 1]) << 8) | (uint8_t)it->buf[i]) << 4) >> 4);
        pos = line_appendf(pos, ",%d", (int16_t)(g * csi));
    }
#else
    if (it->len == 0) {
        return;  /* nothing to print; official code would read buf[0] */
    }
    pos = line_appendf(pos, ",%d,%d,\"[%d", it->len, it->first_word_invalid, (int16_t)(g * it->buf[0]));
    for (int i = 1; i < it->len; i++) {
        pos = line_appendf(pos, ",%d", (int16_t)(g * it->buf[i]));
    }
#endif
    pos = line_appendf(pos, "]\"\n");
    fputs(s_line, stdout);
}

static void print_header(void)
{
    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "================ CSI RECV ================");
#if EG_C5C6_FORMAT
    fputs("type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_format,len,first_word,data\n", stdout);
#else
    fputs("type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data\n", stdout);
#endif
}

static void csi_print_task(void *arg)
{
    bool header_printed = false;
    uint32_t total_at_last = 0;
    int64_t last_stats_us = esp_timer_get_time();

    for (;;) {
        if (xQueueReceive(s_csi_queue, &s_print_item, pdMS_TO_TICKS(100)) == pdTRUE) {
            if (!header_printed) {
                print_header();
                header_printed = true;
            }
            print_csi_item(&s_print_item);
        }

        const int64_t now_us = esp_timer_get_time();
        const int64_t elapsed_us = now_us - last_stats_us;
        if (elapsed_us >= 1000000) {
            const uint32_t total = s_rx_total;
            const float rate_hz = (float)(total - total_at_last) * 1e6f / (float)elapsed_us;
            printf("EG_RX_STATS,%" PRIu32 ",%" PRIu32 ",%.1f,%" PRIu32 ",%" PRIu32 ",%" PRId32 "\n",
                   (uint32_t)(now_us / 1000), total, rate_hz, (uint32_t)s_queue_drops,
                   (uint32_t)s_seq_gaps, (int32_t)s_last_rssi);
            total_at_last = total;
            last_stats_us = now_us;
        }
    }
}

static void wifi_csi_init()
{
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_promiscuous(true));

    /**< default config */
#if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C5 || CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C61
    wifi_csi_config_t csi_config = {
        .enable                   = true,
        .acquire_csi_legacy       = false,
        .acquire_csi_force_lltf   = CSI_FORCE_LLTF,
        .acquire_csi_ht20         = true,
        .acquire_csi_ht40         = true,
        .acquire_csi_vht          = false,
        .acquire_csi_su           = false,
        .acquire_csi_mu           = false,
        .acquire_csi_dcm          = false,
        .acquire_csi_beamformed   = false,
        .acquire_csi_he_stbc_mode = 2,
        .val_scale_cfg            = 0,
        .dump_ack_en              = false,
        .reserved                 = false
    };
#elif CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32C6
    wifi_csi_config_t csi_config = {
        .enable                 = true,
        .acquire_csi_legacy     = false,
        .acquire_csi_ht20       = true,
        .acquire_csi_ht40       = true,
        .acquire_csi_su         = true,
        .acquire_csi_mu         = true,
        .acquire_csi_dcm        = true,
        .acquire_csi_beamformed = true,
        .acquire_csi_he_stbc    = 2,
        .val_scale_cfg          = false,
        .dump_ack_en            = false,
        .reserved               = false
    };
#else
    wifi_csi_config_t csi_config = {
        .lltf_en           = true,
        .htltf_en          = true,
        .stbc_htltf2_en    = true,
        .ltf_merge_en      = true,
        .channel_filter_en = true,
        .manu_scale        = false,
        .shift             = false,
    };
#endif
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_csi_config(&csi_config));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_csi_rx_cb(wifi_csi_rx_cb, NULL));
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_wifi_set_csi(true));
}

static void print_banner(void)
{
    printf("\n");
    printf("==================================================\n");
    printf(" EchoGuard RX (CSI receiver)\n");
    printf(" target        : %s\n", CONFIG_IDF_TARGET);
    printf(" esp-idf       : %s\n", esp_get_idf_version());
    printf(" channel       : %d (HT40, secondary %s)\n", CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL,
           (EG_SECOND_CHAN == WIFI_SECOND_CHAN_BELOW) ? "below" : "above");
    printf(" expected tx   : " MACSTR "\n", MAC2STR(CONFIG_CSI_SEND_MAC));
    printf(" line format   : %s\n", EG_C5C6_FORMAT ? "c5c6 (15 fields)" : "classic (25 fields)");
#if CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY
    printf(" lltf only     : yes (first %d values = 64 subcarriers)\n", EG_COPY_MAX);
#else
    printf(" lltf only     : no (up to %d values)\n", EG_COPY_MAX);
#endif
    printf(" queue depth   : %d\n", CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_QUEUE_LEN);
    printf(" stats line    : EG_RX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<csi_rx_total>,<csi_rx_rate_hz>,<queue_drops>,<seq_gaps>,<last_rssi>\n");
    printf("==================================================\n");
}

void app_main()
{
    /**
     * @brief Initialize NVS
     */
    esp_err_t ret = nvs_flash_init();
    if (ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NO_FREE_PAGES || ret == ESP_ERR_NVS_NEW_VERSION_FOUND) {
        ESP_ERROR_CHECK(nvs_flash_erase());
        ret = nvs_flash_init();
    }
    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(ret);

    print_banner();

    s_csi_queue = xQueueCreate(CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_QUEUE_LEN, sizeof(eg_csi_item_t));
    if (s_csi_queue == NULL) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "failed to allocate CSI queue (%d x %u bytes)",
                 CONFIG_ECHOGUARD_RX_QUEUE_LEN, (unsigned)sizeof(eg_csi_item_t));
        abort();
    }
    /* Lower priority than the Wi-Fi task so printing never starves reception. */
    if (xTaskCreate(csi_print_task, "eg_csi_print", 6144, NULL, 4, NULL) != pdPASS) {
        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "failed to create printer task");
        abort();
    }

    /**
     * @brief Initialize Wi-Fi
     */
    wifi_init();

    /**
     * @brief Initialize ESP-NOW
     *        ESP-NOW protocol see: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/latest/esp32/api-reference/network/esp_now.html
     */

    esp_now_peer_info_t peer = {
        .channel   = CONFIG_LESS_INTERFERENCE_CHANNEL,
        .ifidx     = WIFI_IF_STA,
        .encrypt   = false,
        .peer_addr = {0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff},
    };

    wifi_esp_now_init(peer);

    wifi_csi_init();
}
